sources.cite: Use DAX time intelligence functions in Power BI Desktop models: Additional time intelligence calculations, Microsoft Learn training (updated 2025-06-27)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-16. Relevant text: 'When summarizing snapshot values (like inventory stock levels), you can summarize values across any dimension except date'; 'Adding daily snapshot balances together doesn't produce a meaningful result'; the LASTDATE pattern returns BLANK when no snapshot exists for the last date in filter context ('A recorded date might not exist because it hasn't yet happened'); LASTNONBLANK 'returns the last date that produces a non-BLANK result'. Both measure patterns in the case are the page's.

sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-16. brief.situation: You look after the Inventory report at Ridgeline Outfitters (fictional). The buyers place this month's purchase orders at 15:00 from its Stock on Hand by month. A buyer has just asked why it shows 3,640 Trail Tent 2P in November when the warehouse counts about 150. It is 14:00.

howItWorks: Pick a step from the action list: open or profile something, run a query, a check or a test, change the code or the model, or ship the result. A cell marked with a pencil can be changed by picking a value. Nothing you pick is typed or executed: every step shows an authored result.
Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
The console shows what is open, its flags, charts, tables and code, and the result of each step. 'Read the console' reads it aloud, and every chart can be shown as a table.
Shipping is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the buyers' lead: why the figure was wrong, what the measure does now, and how you checked it.

parts.label: Why it was wrong
parts.criteria: Inventory is a daily balance snapshot; summing it over a month adds about 30 balances. A balance sums across products and warehouses, never across dates.
parts.modelAnswer: SUM over the month added every day's balance: 14 days of November gave 3,640.

parts.label: What it does now
parts.criteria: Takes the balance at the last date that has one (LASTNONBLANK), so a month still in progress shows its latest balance; explains why LASTDATE shows blank and AVERAGE is not a closing balance.
parts.modelAnswer: CALCULATE(SUM(...), LASTNONBLANK('Date'[Date], ...)): 14 Nov for November, 30 Sep and 31 Oct for the others. LASTDATE looks for 30 Nov, which has no row yet.

parts.label: How you checked
parts.criteria: Compared the visual with the latest snapshot rows after the change.
parts.modelAnswer: November shows 150; the 14 Nov snapshot is 150.

scoring.modelReasoning: Inventory holds a daily snapshot of each product's balance, so Stock on Hand is semi-additive: it may sum across products and warehouses but not across dates. SUM over a month adds about 30 balances (3,640 for 14 days of November). AVERAGE gives an average daily balance, not what is on the shelf. LASTDATE takes the balance on the period's last date, which has no snapshot yet for November, so it is blank. CALCULATE with LASTNONBLANK over the dates takes the last date that has a balance: 150, which matches the 14 Nov snapshot.
